extraFacts.fact: Parker builds the 4MA Series NFPA pneumatic tie-rod cylinder in bores of 1-1/2, 2, 2-1/2, 3-1/4, 4, 5, 6 and 8 inch.
extraFacts.source: Parker Hannifin, Pneumatic NFPA Cylinder - 4MA Series product page (ph.parker.com)

extraFacts.fact: Standard 4MA ports are NPTF: 3/8" on the 1-1/2", 2" and 2-1/2" bores, 1/2" on the 3-1/4", 4" and 5" bores and 3/4" on the 6" and 8" bores; BSPP and other port threads are options.
extraFacts.source: Parker Pneumatic Division catalogue 0900P, Tie Rod Cylinders, 4MA port size table

extraFacts.fact: Parker's standard-seal operating temperature for its NFPA tie-rod air cylinders is -10°F to +165°F, which is about -23°C to +74°C.
extraFacts.source: Parker Industrial Cylinder Products catalogue 0106; conversion °C = (°F - 32) / 1.8

extraFacts.fact: 250 psi is about 17 bar and 80 psi is about 5.5 bar (1 bar = 14.5038 psi).

Theoretical extend force of an air cylinder = piston area x pressure, with piston area = pi x bore^2 / 4. Piston areas: 1-1/2" bore 1.77 sq in, 2" 3.14, 2-1/2" 4.91, 3-1/4" 8.3, 4" 12.57, 5" 19.63, 6" 28.27, 8" 50.27. Extend force at 80 psi: 1-1/2" about 141 lbf (64 kgf), 2" 251 lbf (114 kgf), 2-1/2" 393 lbf (178 kgf), 3-1/4" 664 lbf (301 kgf), 4" 1005 lbf (456 kgf), 5" 1571 lbf (713 kgf), 6" 2262 lbf (1026 kgf), 8" 4021 lbf (1824 kgf). Retract force is lower by the rod area, and a load factor of 50 to 75 percent of theoretical force is used for dynamic loads.
extraFacts.source: F = P x A (basic fluid power); Parker Pneumatic Division catalogue 0900P, cylinder force tables and sizing notes

extraFacts.fact: In a Parker NFPA tie-rod cylinder model code the first figure is the bore in inches (e.g. 2.00) and the last figure is the stroke in inches (e.g. 04.00).
extraFacts.source: Parker Pneumatic Division catalogue 0900P, 4MA How to Order / model number breakdown

extraFacts.fact: Parker NFPA tie-rod cylinders are offered with several rod-end thread styles, including small male, intermediate male, full male and short female; a short female rod end has the thread tapped into the end of the piston rod.
extraFacts.source: Parker Industrial Cylinder Products catalogue 0106, rod end styles

extraFacts.fact: The Parker Lipseal piston uses lip-type piston seals that seal on pressure and are suited to non-lubricated air service. A magnetic ring on the piston lets an external reed or solid-state switch sense piston position.
extraFacts.source: Parker Pneumatic Division catalogue 0900P, 4MA standard specifications (Lipseal piston, magnetic piston option)

extraFacts.fact: Linear-acting pneumatic power engines (air cylinders) are classified under HS subheading 8412.31.
extraFacts.source: WCO Harmonized System Nomenclature 2022, heading 84.12, subheading 8412.31
